cues.text: About a thousand years before Christ, Israel had no king. Twelve tribes, bound by a covenant, and judged by an old prophet named Samuel.
Then the elders of Israel came to him at Ramah, and said: “Now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.”
It grieved Samuel. But the LORD said to him: “They have not rejected you, but they have rejected me as the king over them.”
So Israel was given Saul, the son of Kish. From his shoulders and upward he was taller than any of the people.
The LORD sent Saul against Amalek with one command: spare nothing. Saul won the battle. But he spared the king, and the best of the sheep and the cattle.
At Gilgal, Samuel came to him. “Then what does this bleating of the sheep in my ears and the lowing of the cattle which I hear mean? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice.”
As Samuel turned around to go away, Saul grabbed the skirt of his robe, and it tore.
“The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today, and has given it to a neighbour of yours who is better than you.”

Samuel came no more to see Saul until the day of his death. And the LORD said: “Fill your horn with oil, and go. I will send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have provided a king for myself amongst his sons.”
And in Bethlehem, the youngest son was keeping the sheep.
